title: Pinot Grigio and Gewürztraminer
subtitle: Pink-skinned, very different
objectives: Compare Pinot Grigio and Pinot Gris styles
Explain the challenges of aromatic grapes

steps.title: Pinot Grigio and Pinot Gris
steps.body: Pinot Gris has pinkish-grey skin. In north-east Italy it is picked early for light, neutral, crisp Pinot Grigio, one of the world's best-selling whites. In Alsace it is picked riper for fuller, richer wines with pear, honey and spice, sometimes off-dry. Oregon makes a middle style. The name on the label usually signals the style.

steps.title: Gewürztraminer
steps.body: Gewürztraminer, from the Traminer family of north Italy, has pink skin and intense aromas of lychee, rose and ginger, from compounds called terpenes. It ripens to high sugar and often reaches 14% alcohol with low acidity, which can make it feel heavy. Alsace is its home, from dry to late-harvest sweet.
steps.highlight: Lychee and rose, low acidity, high alcohol

steps.prompt: Which aroma is most typical of Gewürztraminer?
steps.explanation: Lychee and rose are Gewürztraminer's signature, from terpenes. Gooseberry points to Sauvignon Blanc.

steps.body: Gewürztraminer is a classic with Munster cheese in Alsace, and its exotic perfume suits mildly spiced dishes, especially when a touch of sweetness balances the heat.

steps.prompt: Gewürztraminer's main challenge is its naturally low ____.
steps.explanation: It ripens to high sugar and alcohol but loses acidity, so growers must pick carefully to keep balance.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Pinot Grigio is light and crisp; Pinot Gris is riper and richer
Gewürztraminer smells of lychee and rose
Aromatic grapes like Gewürztraminer need care to keep acidity
